rationale: Lycopolitan plural form corresponding to Sahidic ⲥⲡⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'lips.' Vowel-insertion ⲥⲟ-ⲁ-ⲡⲉⲧ is consistent with Lycopolitan orthography (cf. ⲥⲁⲡⲉⲧ in line 12 — same root, possibly singular).

proposed_english: to name / to call (lit. 'give a name')
rationale: Verbal idiom ϯ- ('give') + ⲣⲉⲛ/ⲡⲉⲛ ('name'). The Lycopolitan form ⲡⲉⲛ for ⲣⲉⲛ is regular. Idiomatically equivalent to ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'to call.' Used three times on this page (lines 9, 11, 33) in exegetical naming-formulae.
Greek loanword ἀπόφασις — formal judicial pronouncement. With ϯ ('give') = 'pronounce a verdict/sentence.'
Standard Coptic noun for smoke. In Manichaean cosmological context typically signals the realm of darkness or its emanations.
Greek loanword ἑρμηνεύειν with Lycopolitan ⲍ- onset. Used with ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('out, forth') to denote full expository interpretation of a text/symbol.
Standard Coptic verb 'to touch, join.' In line 32 with negation ⲉⲛ → 'not to touch,' suggesting a ritual or exegetical prohibition.
Greek loanword τύπος — 'type, figure, prefiguration.' Standard exegetical term for symbolic/typological reading of scripture; fits this page's tree-typology context.
